Chapter 3: The Role of Education in Shaping Potential.
For a lot of us, school is the very first place where we start to figure out what’s possible—and maybe, what isn’t. The classroom should be a space for discovery, right? But so often, it ends up being a place where curiosity has to squeeze into neat little boxes, just to fit the curriculum.
The way education is set up can either help us search for our Element, or quietly shut that search down.
Take this story—a teenager who absolutely loved music, especially the piano. But her school? They were all about standardized tests. Her passion for playing wasn’t just overlooked—it was actually seen as a distraction from the “real” subjects. Instead of cheering on her talent, she was pushed to spend less time at the piano and more time prepping for exams. The message was loud and clear: creativity comes second to academic scores.
Unfortunately, this isn’t rare. Schools are often designed to deliver predictable outcomes. The goal? Consistency, not individuality. The subjects that are easiest to test—like math, reading, and science—always get top billing. Meanwhile, the arts, PE, and hands-on learning are pushed to the sidelines. So, if you’re one of those students who shines in these areas, it’s easy to feel like your strengths just don’t count.
But here’s the thing—not every educator sees it that way.
There was a teacher who noticed a student’s love for storytelling. Instead of brushing it aside as just a hobby, this teacher encouraged her to write and perform her own plays, right there in class. The result? The student thrived—she grew more confident and started to find her purpose.
These moments of being truly seen can change a life. When someone recognizes your unique spark, you start to believe in your own potential. And sadly, the opposite is true too—if your talents are ignored or dismissed, self-doubt can creep in and take hold.
The way we structure education says a lot about what we value. In many places, the system is built on the belief that intelligence is fixed, and that success means fitting into a narrow mold. But that kind of thinking leaves very little room for different perspectives or experiences.
The world, though, isn’t standing still. The challenges we face today need creativity, adaptability, and skills that can’t be measured by a single test. The people who often make the biggest impact are the ones who think differently, who spot connections others miss, and who aren’t afraid to take a chance.
There’s a great example—a young inventor who just couldn’t connect with traditional subjects. But robotics? That was his thing. Even though his school didn’t offer engineering classes, he taught himself, building machines in his basement. When he finally got to show his work at a science fair, everyone was blown away. His story proves that talent can grow in the most unexpected places—if we just give it a shot.
Education really does have the power to unlock potential—but only if it celebrates the full range of what people can do. That means creating spaces where students can chase their interests, take risks, and even learn from messing up now and then. It means realizing that each person brings something unique to the table, and that the path to fulfillment doesn’t look the same for everyone.
The real challenge? Moving away from a one-size-fits-all approach, and building systems that actually celebrate our differences. When education is designed to nurture the Element, it transforms not just individual lives—but the whole fabric of society.
